name: Trusted Execution Environment Assessment
description: Security assessment of trusted execution environments and hardware-backed isolation. Covers Intel SGX enclave security, ARM TrustZone and Secure World assessment, AMD SEV-SNP and Intel TDX confidential computing evaluation, TPM-based attestation and sealing, Apple Secure Enclave Processor, and remote attestation protocol analysis. Evaluation of TPM hardware and hardware roots of trust belongs to HWSEC-EMBED-TPM.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to trusted execution environment assessment

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands TEE architectures and hardware-backed isolation concepts
evidence: Can explain Intel SGX, ARM TrustZone, and AMD SEV at an architectural level
Understands TPM attestation, sealing, and remote attestation concepts
Familiar with the threat models TEEs address and their limitations
Completed introductory training on trusted execution environments

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Evaluates TEE configurations and reviews attestation under supervision
evidence: Reviewed SGX enclave configurations and attestation evidence
Assessed TPM-based Measured Boot and sealing policies
Tested basic TEE side-channel attack concepts in lab environment
Work reviewed by authorized researcher

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses TEE implementations and attestation chains
evidence: Independently assessed SGX or TrustZone implementations in 3+ engagements
Evaluates remote attestation protocols for correctness and replay vulnerabilities
Identifies enclave interface attack surface and sealing weaknesses
Passed proficiency assessment on TEE security

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Exploits TEE weaknesses; evaluates confidential computing platforms
evidence: Performs side-channel attacks against SGX enclaves (cache timing, page fault)
Evaluates confidential computing platforms (Azure CC, GCP Confidential VMs)
Assesses enclave code for information leakage and interface vulnerabilities
Mentors team on TEE assessment methodology

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Authority on TEE security; published enclave or attestation research
evidence: Published research on SGX, TrustZone, or confidential computing vulnerabilities
Developed lab methodology for TEE security assessment
Contributes to confidential computing security guidance
Trains teams and presents at conferences on TEE exploitation

assessment_methods.description: Assess an SGX enclave application for interface vulnerabilities and side-channel exposure in a lab environment
Given a remote attestation protocol specification, identify weaknesses and propose attack scenarios
